description: §5.2.3's invalid worked example verbatim — a BARE (unbraced) `onclick=` handler whose value is two semicolon-separated expressions fires E-MULTI-STATEMENT-HANDLER. This is the shape the S435 L19 reversal NARROWED the code to (the braced inline block is legal — see `inline-block-handler-runs-every-statement`). W-DEAD-FUNCTION / W-PROGRAM-001 co-fire incidentally; not asserted.
rationale: §5.2.3 (amended S435, L19 reversed): "A BARE (unbraced) event-handler value SHALL contain exactly one scrml expression" and "A BARE event-handler value that contains a `;` outside of expression-internal contexts (string literals, template literals, parentheses, brackets, braces, nested function bodies, comments) is compile error `E-MULTI-STATEMENT-HANDLER`. The fix is to wrap the statements in braces". The source is §5.2.3's own "Worked example — invalid (unbraced statement sequence)": `<button onclick=startGame(); track("start")>Begin</>`. The `;` sits at top level of the opener's attribute region, with no braces around the handler, and its owning attribute `onclick` is in the event-handler family, so the code SHALL fire.
